summary: This CSS file styles a code snippet component with collapsible syntax-highlighted content. It defines the visual layout and appearance of the snippet container, toolbar with language logos, and an optional line-by-line explanation feature (ELI5). Each language gets its own brand color that appears as a top border and in the language icon.

explanations.42: This uses CSS Modules composition to inherit styles from a global 'mk-surface' class, pulling in predefined base styles for this element.
explanations.80: The :has() selector applies padding changes only when a <pre> tag exists inside—removing padding because the <pre> adds its own.
explanations.94: The !important flag forces the background to be transparent even if other CSS rules try to set a background color, ensuring the dark ground below shows through.
explanations.108: This creates a semi-transparent white overlay (0.06 opacity) using rgba() with a percentage-based alpha channel.
explanations.137: If --lang-color isn't defined on an element, it falls back to the site's primary color; this provides a sensible default for snippets without a language variant class.
explanations.164: The chevron rotates based on the --chevron-rotation variable, which is set to 180deg when the snippet expands.
explanations.194: The logo color uses --lang-color if available, otherwise falls back to a neutral gray (--mk-n-500) for languages without a specific brand color.
explanations.205: This drop-shadow filter adds a subtle dark outline to light-colored logos so they remain visible against the light toolbar background.
explanations.223: Every variant_ class inherits this base rule, which sets a neutral gray color before being overridden by specific language colors below.
explanations.356: The hover state uses a very subtle white overlay (4% opacity) to show feedback without dramatically changing the code appearance.
explanations.394: The background uses a semi-transparent green (14% opacity) to create a subtle badge tint using the terminal prompt color.
explanations.446: The :where() pseudo-class wrapper has zero specificity, so it won't accidentally override the button's own hover styles defined earlier.
explanations.471: This positions the tooltip above the triggering element by moving it up by its full height plus 8px of gap.
